The granted account is deleted at **2026-10-27 13:38 UTC**. The planned generation
cutoff is 09:37 UTC and closeout cutoff is 12:38 UTC that day. These are absolute

The allocation is one NVIDIA L4 (23,034 MiB) on a four-GPU shared host with an

Eight CPU workers, one BLAS thread

Systemd user lingering is enabled for this temporary account so services survive

The source is pinned to `1937c7ba11e045449ef5469685b405ab51da58f3`, Python 3.11.15
and the 99 hashed qualification packages. The bootstrap installer was updated
from uv 0.9.25 to 0.13.5 because the older catalogue did not contain Python 3.11.15;

These checks do not establish full-pilot completion or a runtime estimate.

Jupyter's provider cgroup permits `/dev/nvidia1`, UUID
`GPU-4f1bade3-abd9-f729-e94d-05f052d21d40`. An SSH login sees all four GPUs,
so the first Moirai measurement refused before generation. The persistent
service must set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to that full UUID and use an operational

This scopes real probe/sampler output to the allocation; it does not reproduce
the provider's device-access isolation. Preserve the unfiltered inventory,
provider policy, launcher hash, selected-device probe and failed attempt.
The source checkout and all canonical job identities remain unchanged.

## Cloud checkpoint protocol

The temporary `pilot-l4-checkpoints.yml` workflow runs every 20 minutes during
the grant, and can also be dispatched manually. It uses an ephemeral account SSH
key stored as an encrypted repository Actions secret. GitHub credentials stay on
the hosted runner. No laptop relay is required.

`scripts/pilot_checkpoint.py` captures two alternating local snapshot slots with
an atomic receipt published last. Each snapshot contains cumulative cache
partitions, refreshed native events/resource logs, operational scripts, admission
evidence and completed closeout archives. The already published
`pilot-resume-2026-10-23` base archive supplies unchanged original inputs; its
SHA-256 is fixed in each snapshot manifest. Source data and model weights are not
downloaded again for backups. Credentials, symlinks and temporary writes are excluded.

The workflow verifies the archive digest and every captured file, uploads uniquely
named release assets, downloads them again and re-verifies them. Only then does
it acknowledge the snapshot to the remote watchdog. A snapshot is a file-by-file
recovery point, **not** an atomic filesystem image or a passing forecast audit.
Restore the pinned base archive, overlay a verified snapshot into the matching
workspace, relocate only source paths if needed, then run the normal cache audit.

The remote watchdog stops the forecast service if the last cloud-verified snapshot
is an hour old, a phase deadline is reached, an OOM event occurs, or less than
5 GiB of shared disk remains. GitHub scheduled jobs may be delayed; a missed-backup
stop preserves evidence and requires an explicit reviewed resume. It is not
silently restarted. The workflow disables itself after account expiry.

The checkpoint release remains a partial operational archive. Full pilot audit,
zero-generation rerun, disposable recovery, resource accounting and both actual
consumer acceptances remain the completion conditions. Follow
[pilot-closeout.md](../../runbooks/pilot-closeout.md).
